title: Children's and pupils' data (EU)
description: Questions for the privacy, product and legal owners and repository checks for services used by children or pupils in the EU: GDPR Art. 8, 12 and 35, Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) Art. 28 for online platforms, and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Annex III point 3 for AI in education. Each Member State sets its own age of consent and education law; these rules do not establish compliance.

sources.title: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk, Annex III: high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)

rules.instruction: Ask the privacy owner whether children use the service, in which Member States, and which age of consent each one sets for information society services under GDPR Art. 8(1): 16, or lower by law but not below 13.
rules.verification: Link the recorded age for each Member State from the change.

rules.instruction: When consent is the lawful basis and the child is below that age, make the flow obtain consent given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility (GDPR Art. 8(1)).
rules.verification: Run the test where an account below the age cannot go on without a recorded parental consent.

rules.instruction: Write the privacy information and notices shown to children in clear and plain language they can understand (GDPR Art. 12(1)).
rules.verification: Link the privacy owner's recorded review of the new texts.

rules.instruction: Ask the data protection officer whether processing children's or pupils' data in the change requires a data protection impact assessment under GDPR Art. 35(1), and record the decision with its reason.
rules.verification: Link the assessment, or the recorded reason it is not required, from the change.

rules.instruction: When the product is an online platform accessible to minors, ask the product owner which measures give minors a high level of privacy, safety and security (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 Art. 28(1)), such as private default settings, and implement them.
rules.verification: Check the default settings of a new minor account against the recorded measures.

rules.instruction: When the product is an online platform, do not present advertising based on profiling with personal data to a user known with reasonable certainty to be a minor (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 Art. 28(2)).
rules.verification: Run the test that requests advertising for an account flagged as a minor and finds no profiling-based targeting, or link the record that the service shows no advertising.

rules.instruction: When an AI feature determines admission, evaluates learning outcomes, assesses the level of education or monitors students during tests, ask the legal owner whether it is high-risk under AI Act Annex III point 3, and select the eu-ai-act-system pattern when it is.
rules.verification: Link the recorded classification from the change.
